text: For the rest, the standard library has types that own their contents in other ways, each with a cost: Type What it gives you Cost Python analogue Box<T> one owner, value on the heap; needed for recursive types and trait objects one allocation every object Rc<T> shared ownership in one thread; freed when the last Rc goes a counter update per clone and drop reference counting Arc<T> the same across threads atomic counter updates (slower) reference counting in free-threaded CPython Cell<T> , RefCell<T> interior mutability : change through a shared reference; RefCell checks the borrow rules at run time a flag check per borrow; a panic if the rules are broken (all objects are mutable) Mutex<T> , RwLock<T> the same across threads, by locking a lock per access; contention threading.Lock Weak<T> a non-owning pointer to an Rc / Arc value; breaks cycles upgrade() may find it gone weakref A recursive type needs Box , because a value that contains itself directly would have infinite size; with the Box each child is one 8-byte pointer, as the run below prints ( size_of Box<Expr> = 8 ).
